# Hostages – Amiga port to C++/SDL2

Port of the Amiga version of **Hostages** (Infogrames, 1989; also known as
*Operation Jupiter* / *Embassy Mission*) to C++ and SDL2.

The game's original 68000 code runs on a small runtime that provides
exactly what the code expects from an Amiga 500, so no Kickstart ROM and no
extracted files are needed – the game boots straight from the original disk
image. Two releases are supported:

- **Hostage** (`Hostage (Infogrames).adf`): Infogrames' trackloader disk
  (custom bootblock, own file directory, manual word check, rank access
  codes);
- **Hostages** (`Hostages (1988)(Infogrames)[cr].adf`): the European release
  as a cracked AmigaDOS disk (startup-sequence runs `apro1.` and then
  `it.`, an Intuition screen, no checks). It has the "HOSTAGES" logo, the
  mission "JUPITER" instead of "ASSAULT" and different intro music.

What is emulated:

- the parts of Kickstart the game uses, emulated at the library level:
  exec (memory with real MemHeaders, lists, ports, signals, interrupt
  servers, devices), trackdisk.device on the ADF, the boot strap that runs
  the bootblock, or for an AmigaDOS disk a CLI that executes
  s/startup-sequence, dos.library on the disk's OFS file system (Open/Read/
  Lock/Examine/LoadSeg…), Intuition screens/windows and the graphics.library
  calls used (RastPort drawing, BltBitMap, LoadRGB4, AllocRaster…);
- the custom chips the game programs directly: copper and bitplane display,
  sprites, blitter, Paula audio DMA, disk DMA, the two CIAs (keyboard,
  joystick fire, music timer, drive control).

The manual word check of "Hostage" ("enter word N on line N of page N") is
bypassed by default, much like a WHDLoad install patch: any answer,
including just Return, is accepted. `--skip-codes` also skips the secret
access codes for the CAPTAIN and COMMANDER ranks (the end screens give
them: HPETS for Captain, EDUAB for Commander); "Hostages" has no codes.

## Requirements

One of the two disk images (not included). The game looks for them in the
current directory, `assets/` and the install data dir, or the ADF can be
given on the command line.

## Support matrix

| Target | Artifact | Command |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Linux desktop (SDL2) | package + `.desktop` / AppStream | `nix build` / `nix run` |
| Windows x86_64 / i686 | folder or zip (MinGW + SDL2.dll) | `nix build .#hostages-win64` / `.#hostages-win64-zip` |
| WebAssembly | static site (html/js/wasm) | `nix build .#hostages-wasm` / `nix run .#hostages-wasm` |
| R36S / ArkOS (PortMaster) | port tree or zip | `nix build .#hostages-r36s-portmaster` / `.#hostages-r36s-portmaster-zip` |
| Android | signed debug APK | `nix build .#hostages-android` / `nix run .#hostages-android-install` |

All targets require a **user-supplied, non-redistributable ADF**. Version source: top-level `VERSION` (`0.1.0-dev`); Nix development builds append `.<revCount>+g<rev>`.

## Build

```bash
nix develop
hostages-configure && hostages-build
hostages-run [disk.adf]          # or: hostages-run-gdb
# in-tree still works:
cmake -B build && cmake --build build
./build/hostages
```

Package / one-shot:

```bash
nix build                         # Linux: result/bin/hostages + desktop files
nix build .#checks.version
nix run . -- --version
nix build .#hostages-win64-zip
nix build .#hostages-wasm
nix build .#hostages-r36s-portmaster-zip
nix build .#hostages-android
```

Requires one of the two non-redistributable ADF images (see above).

## Running

```
hostages [options] [disk.adf]
  --scale N        window scale (default 3)
  --state-dir DIR  written disk + save states (default $XDG_STATE_HOME/hostages;
                   falls back to $XDG_DATA_HOME/hostages if present)
  --save DIR       alias for --state-dir (legacy)
  -V, --version    print version
  --show-paths     print resolved paths and exit
  --speed X        CPU speed multiplier (default 1 = A500)
  --protection     keep the manual word check
  --skip-codes     accept any rank access code
  --fast           run unthrottled
```

Developer options: `--verbose` (log OS calls), `--trace`, `--frames N`,
`--screenshot N file.ppm`, `--script file`, `--wav file`, `--coverage file`,
`--ram-hash N` (see `hostages --help` and AGENTS.md).

## Controls

The game is played with a joystick in port 2, the keyboard, or a gamepad:

| Input | Function |
|-------|----------|
| Cursor keys / game controller stick / D-pad | joystick (the game also reads the cursor keys itself) |
| Right Ctrl / Space / controller A | fire |
| Return / controller X or Start | confirm / next screen / continue |
| F1–F6 | select team member (DELTA…BRAVO); on a gamepad use **Y (North)** to open the team menu instead |
| F10 | restart current stage (on gamepad: team menu → Restart when stage I targets are set) |
| F11 | fullscreen |
| Pause | fast forward |
| F9 / controller Back | debug menu (save states, stage I complete, …) |
| Controller Y (North) | team select menu (stage I: DELTA/ECHO/MIKE; stage II: all six; when stage I targets are set also Continue / Restart) |
| Controller B (East) | Esc (stage II map / gameplay screen toggle) |
| L/R shoulder | F1 / F2 |

## License

GPLv3+ for the new code. The game itself is not included and not
redistributable; this is a reverse-engineering / preservation project.

grumbel-turrican2-port-readme-md.text:
# Turrican II – Amiga port to C++/SDL2

Port of the Amiga version of **Turrican II: The Final Fight** (Factor 5 /
Rainbow Arts, 1991) to C++ and SDL2.

The game's original 68000 code runs on a small runtime that provides what
the code expects from an Amiga 500 (no Kickstart ROM needed): the parts of
exec/trackdisk.device the bootblock and intro use, emulated at library
level, and the custom chips the game programs directly (copper and
display, sprites, blitter, Paula, disk DMA, CIAs). The game boots straight
from the original disk image.

Plan: static recompilation of the 68000 code first (as in the FA-18
Interceptor port), then a native reimplementation with new features
(gamepad support, …).

## Requirements

The original disk image `T2.adf` (extended ADF, not included).

## Build

```bash
nix develop          # or: install cmake, a C++20 compiler and SDL2
cmake -B build
cmake --build build
./build/turrican2 T2.adf
```

## Controls

| Input | Function |
|-------|----------|
| Cursor keys / left stick / D-pad | joystick in port 2 (move / jump / duck) |
| Right Ctrl | fire (hold = surround shot after a moment, as in the game) |
| Gamepad **Y** | fire (hold = surround shot; at once with the *Instant surround* cheat) |
| Gamepad **A** | jump (joystick up) |
| Gamepad **X** | auto-fire (pulsed fire taps) |
| Gamepad **B** / Space | powerline (secondary); down+B = gyroscope |
| Gamepad **Back** / Esc | quit to intro |
| Gamepad **Start** | open host debug menu (D-pad navigate, A ok, B cancel; L/R adjust) |
| Ctrl | pause (fire to resume) |
| F11 / Alt-Enter | fullscreen |
| Pause | fast forward |

### Debug menu (Start)

Host-side overlay; the game is paused while it is open (game actions take
effect on resume). B goes back from the cheats page, and closes the menu
on the main page.

Main page: resume, restart, give up (Esc, as in the game), **Cheats >**,
always auto-fire, freeze, **centre display** (on by default: the area the
Amiga displays, taken from its display window and data fetch registers,
is centred in the window; off shows the Amiga's own position), and
**10 save-state slots** (Save / Load), stored under the save directory as
`states/slotN.t2ss`.

Cheats page (uses the decoded memory map of the game, docs/memory_map.md,
and the game's own routines, so the HUD follows):

- **Level select** (left/right: 1-1 … 5-2): in a game it warps there at
  once (through the game's stage-complete path); on the title screen the
  next game starts there
- **Weapon** (left/right: Multiple 0–2, Laser 0–4, Rebound 0–3), max all
  weapons
- extra life, lives = 99, infinite lives, full energy, infinite energy,
  god mode (no damage; the timer stops too), instant surround on Y (also
  in the air; off by default), refill power line, wheel
  bombs = 99, continues = 5, time = 999, the game's built-in cheat flag
  (no life loss, no score)

## License

GPLv3+ for the new code. The game itself is not included and not
redistributable; this is a reverse-engineering / preservation project.

pbl64k-color-snake-classic-readme-md.text:
# Color Snake Classic

Color Snake Classic is a faithful modern restoration of L. Lepin's original MSX
game *Color Snake*, described as “a strange hybrid of Color Lines, Snake, and
Tetris.” The original Z80 source was lost; this repository reconstructs the game
from the surviving 9 KB MSX-DOS executable, emulator experiments, recovered
assets, and the Lepin family's design recollections.

The repository contains both the playable Godot port and the digital-archaeology
record used to establish the original behavior. Start with the
[documentation map](docs/README.md) for the evidence trail.
The [reproducibility guide](docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md) explains how to regenerate
the deliberately excluded analysis and release artifacts.

## Run from source

Requirements:

- Windows 10 or later
- [Godot 4.7.2 Standard](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/4.7.2-stable/)
- PowerShell 5.1 or later

Clone the repository, then either add Godot to `PATH` and run:

```powershell
.\Run-Game.ps1
```

or give the executable explicitly:

```powershell
.\Run-Game.ps1 -GodotExecutable C:\Tools\Godot\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe
```

There are no package dependencies, generated source files, or required external
assets. Godot imports the checked-in resources on first launch.

The historical clean presentation is the default. An optional CRT filter and a
buffered-input mode can be selected explicitly before starting a run.

## Test

```powershell
.\Test.ps1
```

The presentation-independent suite covers recovered rules, timing, both game
modes, persistence, input policy, controller flow, sound synthesis, and the fixed
historical tail-growth match fault.

## Build release packages

Install the matching Godot 4.7.2 export templates through the Godot editor and
ensure Python 3 is available for deterministic icon generation. For the optional
Windows installer, install [Inno Setup 7](https://jrsoftware.org/isdl.php). Then
run:

```powershell
.\Build-Release.ps1
```

The script tests first, exports the embedded-PCK Windows executable and
single-threaded itch.io web build, creates both ZIPs, compiles the installer when
`ISCC.exe` is available, and writes SHA-256 checksums under `build/release/`.
Both Godot and Inno Setup can also be supplied with `-GodotExecutable` and
`-InnoCompiler`.

## Archaeology and repository policy

- `snk.com` is the preserved primary binary and is intentionally tracked.
- `analysis/` contains reproducible extraction, emulator, state-injection, and
  summarization scripts plus compact probe definitions.
- `assets/recovered/` contains small exact or deterministically rendered assets
  required by the port, with hashes and provenance.
- `docs/` contains durable findings; generated traces are not evidence by
  themselves and are not committed.
- `analysis/generated/`, `build/`, `tooling/`, `work/`, `.godot/`, and the large
  `snake.avi` recording are excluded from Git.

The source, recovered assets, and distributable builds are released under the
[MIT License](LICENSE) with authorization from the original author.

missingno7-secret-agent-editor-readme-md.text:
# Secret Agent Editor

A small Python reverse-engineering viewer and level editor for Apogee's
**Secret Agent** game data.

The editor works with already-extracted game files. It intentionally does not
handle installer archives or SHR extraction. Point it at a `game_data` folder,
or at a ZIP that contains the final game files:

```text
SAM101.GFX / SAM201.GFX / SAM301.GFX  # 16x16 tile banks
SAM103.GFX / SAM203.GFX / SAM303.GFX  # level archives
```

## Features

- Loads episodes 1, 2, and 3 when their data files are present.
- Decodes the Secret Agent XOR/bit-reversal encryption used by map and tile
  files.
- Decodes ProGraphx `tls-sagent-8k` 16x16 EGA tiles.
- Renders normal levels and the world map using the Camoto/SAMLEV-derived
  map-code to tile mapping.
- Supports foreground `*` rows as overlays on the previous visual row.
- Provides a Tkinter GUI with zoom, scrollable maps, grid/raw-code/unknown-code
  overlays, cell inspection, background/foreground painting, a visual map-code
  picker, and a raw tile-bank atlas.
- Saves edited encrypted `SAM?03.GFX` level archives.
- Offers CLI helpers for PNG previews and raw map-code dumps.

## Requirements

- Python 3.10 or newer
- Pillow
- Tkinter, included with most desktop Python distributions

Install the runtime dependency directly:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Or install the project in editable mode:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

## Usage

Run the GUI without installing the package:

```bash
python main.py path/to/game_data
```

You can also open a ZIP that contains the extracted game data:

```bash
python main.py path/to/game_data.zip
```

After editable installation, the console command is available too:

```bash
secret-agent-editor path/to/game_data
```

If no path is provided, the app looks for `game_data` or `game_data.zip` in the
current working directory.

## CLI Helpers

Export a rendered PNG preview:

```bash
python main.py game_data.zip --episode 1 --level 3 --export-preview ep1_level03.png --zoom 1 --no-unknown
```

Dump the raw map codes used by one level:

```bash
python main.py game_data.zip --episode 1 --level 3 --dump-codes
```

Useful options:

- `--episode N`: episode number, usually `1`, `2`, or `3`
- `--level N`: level index, where `0` is the world map
- `--zoom N`: preview export scale
- `--codes`: draw raw map codes on exported previews
- `--no-unknown`: hide unknown-code markers on exported previews

## Editor Notes

- The map-code picker reflows automatically when the right panel or window is
  resized.
- Empty source-derived bank categories are hidden from the picker.
- Hold Shift while moving over the level grid to preview the currently selected
  map code as a ghost placement overlay.
- Shift + left click paints the selected code to the active background or
  foreground layer.
- Right click clears the active layer cell. Background cells become `0x20`;
  foreground cells become `0x00`.
- The raw `SAM?01.GFX` bank atlas remains available as a separate tab for
  reverse-engineering and debugging.

## Project Layout

```text
secret_agent_editor/
  crypto.py      # Secret Agent encryption/decryption helpers
  graphics.py    # ProGraphx EGA tile decoding
  levels.py      # 2016-byte level block parsing and encoding
  mapping.py     # Map-code to bank/tile references
  render.py      # Level renderer
  gui.py         # Tkinter GUI
  cli.py         # CLI entry point
```

Additional reverse-engineering notes live in `docs/`, including current engine
research leads from OpenCrystalCaves and the Secret Agent disassembly.

## Data And Legal Notes

This repository does not include Secret Agent game data. Use your own legally
obtained copy and keep extracted data files outside version control.

grumbel-fa18-interceptor-port-readme-md.text:
# F/A-18 Interceptor – Modern Port

Port of the 1988 Amiga flight simulator **F/A-18 Interceptor**
(Bob Dinnerman / Intellisoft, Electronic Arts) to C++ and SDL2.

The game's original 68000 code is statically recompiled to C++ at build time
and runs on top of a small runtime that provides what the code expects from
an Amiga 500: the handful of AmigaOS calls it makes (exec, dos, graphics,
intuition and the keyboard/timer/gameport/audio devices) and the custom
chips it programs directly (copper/bitplane display, blitter line and fill
drawing, Paula sound). A 68000 interpreter is kept as fallback and as a
reference; both produce bit-identical frames and audio.

The complete game works: title, enlistment, demo flight, free flight,
training, qualification, missions and the flight log (saved to disk).

## Requirements

The original game disk image (ADF), e.g. the TOSEC dump
`FA-18 Interceptor (1988)(Electronic Arts).adf`. The ADF is **not** shipped
with this repository and must not be committed to it — pass its path at
runtime and (for a recompiled build) to CMake.

The runtime opens the ADF directly; there is no need to unpack the disk into
an `assets/` directory. A legacy directory of unpacked files is still
accepted if you already have one.

The ADF is only needed at **runtime** (pass it as the data argument). Build
does not require it: without an original executable CMake builds the
interpreter-only binary. Optional static recompilation needs the executable
once at build time (`-DFA18_EXE=...`, or `-DFA18_ADF=...` to extract it).


## Platforms

Desktop Linux remains the primary target. Additional ports (scaffolded after
[kurvenrausch](https://github.com/Grumbel/kurvenrausch)):

| Package | Command | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| WebAssembly | `nix build .#fa18-wasm` / `nix run .#fa18-wasm` | Upload ADF in the browser (IDBFS); not embedded |
| Windows 64/32 | `nix build .#fa18-win64` | MinGW + official SDL2 MinGW DLLs |
| R36S / ArkOS | `nix build .#fa18-r36s` | PortMaster launcher; place ADF in the port folder |
| Android | `nix build .#fa18-android` | APK; `adb push disk.adf` into app files dir |

The original ADF is never redistributed. See `TODO.md` for open port work.

## Build

```bash
nix develop          # or: install cmake, SDL2, python3
cmake -B build
cmake --build build
./build/fa18 "FA-18 Interceptor (1988)(Electronic Arts).adf"
```

or `nix build && ./result/bin/fa18 path/to/game.adf`.

## Running

```
fa18 [options] [data]
  data           path to the original .adf, or a directory of unpacked
                 disk files (default: looks for a nearby .adf / ./assets)
  --speed X      CPU speed (default 4: the game caps itself at 15 fps;
                 1 = stock A500, 6-8 fps in flight and slower simulation)
  --save DIR     config / flight log directory
                 (default $XDG_DATA_HOME/fa18-interceptor)
  --scale N      window scale
  --protection   keep the codewheel check (default: bypassed like the
                 WHDLoad install)
  --interpret    use the 68000 interpreter instead of recompiled code
```

Developer options: `--fast`, `--frames N`, `--screenshot N file.ppm`,
`--script file`, `--wav file`, `--coverage file`, `--misses file`,
`--verbose`, `--trace` (see `fa18 --help` and AGENTS.md).

## Controls

Keys are passed to the game as on the Amiga (see `manual.txt`):

| Key | Function |
|-----|----------|
| Cursor keys | Fly (up = nose down, down = nose up, left/right = roll) |
| F1–F10, `=` / `-` | Throttle (F10 twice = afterburner) |
| Space / Return | Fire / select weapon |
| `,` `.` | Rudder |
| G, A, Backspace | Gear, arrestor hook, brakes |
| H, J, C, F, M, R, T | HUD, ECM, chaff, flare, map, radar range, target |
| Keypad | View directions; Keypad Enter = outside view |
| `[` `]` | Zoom |
| P, Esc, Shift-Esc | Pause, restart, back to mission selection |

Front end keys: **F11** fullscreen, **Pause** fast-forward, **F12**
captures the mouse (port 1; the game reads it but flies with joystick or
keyboard).

### Game controller

The original Amiga game only supports a **digital** joystick (four
directions + fire on port 2) — it never reads the proportional pot
registers.  The left stick is therefore thresholded to digital
directions.  Remaining functions are mapped to buttons and two hold
layers that work like pie menus (hold the shoulder, push the stick
into a direction: the entry fires immediately; click the stick for the
centre entry):

| Input | Action |
|-------|--------|
| Left stick / D-pad | Fly |
| A | Fire |
| B | Select weapon |
| X | Cycle target |
| Y | Map |
| LT / RT | Throttle down / up |
| Start / Back | Pause / debug menu (see below) |
| LS click / RS click | Brakes / Gear |
| Right stick X / Y | Rudder / Zoom |
| **LB + stick** (push) | Systems pie: N radar, E target, S map, W HUD, NE ECM, SE chaff, SW flare, NW arrestor, stick click = gear |
| **LB + face** | A HUD, B ECM, X chaff, Y flare |
| **RB + stick** (push) | View pie (keypad directions); stick click = forward, **RB+A** = outside view |

### Remaster options and debug menu

All off by default; the original behaviour is untouched.

- `--hires N`: render the 3D view at N times resolution (HUD and cockpit
  stay low-res).
- `FA18_SCENE_RENDER=<N>`: software hi-res path from the captured
  `SceneFrame` — depth-sorts all prims (fills, polys, lines, points),
  rasterizes them at N× into the 3D view, then pastes only HUD/cockpit
  rows from the low-res frame.  Incomplete capture shows as missing
  geometry (not papered over by the original low-res 3D).  Observation
  only.  Implies scene capture.  `--hires` takes priority if both are set.
- `--analog`: left stick flies analog (dead zone, proportional pitch and
  rudder) instead of the thresholded digital directions.
- `--text-pace`: menu texts, briefings and cockpit messages at the pace of
  a stock A500 (they otherwise run several times faster; the game itself
  is not slowed down, see docs/frame_timing.md).
- **Back** (keyboard: Insert) opens the debug menu: 3D resolution, analog
  stick, text pacing, save/load state slots and a way to send ESC to the game.  Save
  states are stored next to the flight log; they can also be loaded from
  the intro.

## Project layout

- `src/m68k/` – 68000 interpreter and shared ALU semantics
- `src/amiga/` – machine model, custom chips, OS high-level emulation
- `src/recomp/` – interface to the generated code
- `tools/` – ADF/hunk tools, disassembler, recompiler (`recomp.py`)
- `tests/cpu_sst.cpp` – CPU conformance test (SingleStepTests 68000)
- `docs/` – reverse-engineering notes

## License

New code: GPLv3+. The original game remains under its original copyright;
this is an educational reverse-engineering project.

opencol-mapedit-readme-md.text:
# mapedit-port

The **Colonization Map Editor** (`MAPEDIT.EXE`, MicroProse 1994) running natively on Windows,
macOS and Linux. It is built from [mapedit-decomp](https://github.com/OpenCol/mapedit-decomp), the editor's source
recovered from the shipped program, compiled with modern compilers, and it runs on
[SDL3](https://libsdl.org) instead of DOS.

**Status: 0.1.0, faithful.** The editor runs natively on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel)
and Windows (64-bit), and Linux builds from source. Given the same keys, it writes `.MP` files
byte-identical to the original's running under DOSBox-X (`tools/m4.py`, six sessions: open
and save, paint, undo, fill, Find Continents, a new map). Improvements come next, each
behind an option. [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md) has the milestones.

## Download

[Releases](https://github.com/OpenCol/mapedit/releases): `mapedit-<version>-macos.zip`
(an application, "Colonization Map Editor.app") and `mapedit-<version>-windows-x64.zip`
(`mapedit.exe` and `SDL3.dll`). Each has a README.txt on starting it. You need your own
copy of *Colonization* for DOS (GOG or Steam): the editor asks for its folder the first
time and remembers it.

On macOS the app is not notarized: the first time, right-click it and choose Open.

## The code

Four layers -- `src/sys`, `src/core`, `src/ui`, `src/editor` -- each using only those below
it, with one header per subsystem in `src/include`; [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)
has the map and the checks that keep it so.

## What you need

- your own copy of *Colonization* for DOS (GOG or Steam). The editor reads the game's art,
  fonts and palette from it, and none of that is in this repository;
- CMake 3.16 or later, a C99 compiler, and SDL3.

```sh
cmake -B build && cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build                      # self-tests; the oracle with MAPEDIT_EXE set
```

Run it on a copy of your game directory -- the editor writes its maps there, as it did:

```sh
build/mapedit --game /path/to/COLONIZE
build/mapedit --game /path/to/COLONIZE --headless --script session.txt
```

Without `--game` (or `$MAPEDIT_GAME`) it looks in the current directory, then its own (or,
for the macOS app, the folder the app is in), then the folder chosen last time, and else
asks with a folder dialog (`--choose-game` asks again). On macOS, `cmake --build build
--target mapedit_app` makes "Colonization Map Editor.app"; `tools/release.py` builds the
release zips (a static, universal SDL3 for the app; the Windows build cross-compiled).

### Windows

With MSYS2 (UCRT64: `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-{gcc,cmake,ninja,sdl3,python}`):

```sh
cmake -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build --target mapedit
```

`build/mapedit.exe` and `build/SDL3.dll` are the program. From macOS or Linux, cross-build
with MinGW-w64 and SDL3's MinGW development package (`cmake/mingw-w64-x86_64.cmake` says
how); `tools/m4.py --wine` checks the result under Wine. MSVC builds too (CI).

A script is one command a line: `wait MS`, `key NAME`, `type TEXT`, `move X Y`, `click X Y`,
`shot FILE.bmp`, `exit` (platform/host_sdl.c has them all).

The oracle tests run the player's own `MAPEDIT.EXE` in an emulator beside the port: set
`MAPEDIT_EXE` to it and install Python's `unicorn` package.

## The contract

The port must behave exactly like the 1994 program before it does anything new. Given the
same input, it shows the same screens and writes byte-identical `.MP` files. Gate M4
([docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md)) measures that against the original running under DOSBox-X.
Improvements come after it, each behind an option.

## Improvements

Each is off unless asked for on the command line, so the editor stays the 1994 program by
default (`src/include/options.h` has the details):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `--undo N` | Undo goes back through the last N changes (the original keeps one, of the terrain only), Map > Redo Last Change (R) goes forward again; Ctrl-Z and Ctrl-Y |
| `--check-save` | before a save: Find Continents runs, and a popup lists what the game would change or mind (no land, land in the columns the game makes sea lane, one-square rivers) and asks whether to save anyway |
| `--export-png [DIR]` | Editor > Export Map as PNG (E): the whole map at full zoom, in DIR or the current folder |
| `--new-map-menu` | the editor starts with New empty map / Load existing map (and Generate random map where the program around it has the game's generator: OpenCol), instead of the file list; Editor > Create Map offers the same |
| `--improved` | all four, with 64 steps of Undo |
| `--save-dir DIR` | maps are written to DIR; the game directory is then only read (DIR's files first) |
| `--play` | Editor > Play This Map in Game (G), for a program that starts the editor: the map is saved and the editor ends, printing `play NAME.MP` |
| `--test-generator` | Generate random map with a stand-in generator (one rectangle of land), for the tests |

# Prehistorik 2 reconstruction

A readable TASM source of the DOS game Prehistorik 2 (`PRE2.EXE`, Titus 1993, written in
assembly by Eric Zmiro) that assembles to the exact original program, and a C translation
of it that is verified against that source routine by routine, on the way to a native
SDL3 port.

```
PRE2.EXE  <- byte exact ->  src/ (semantic ASM oracle)  <- differential tests ->  c/  ->  host/ (SDL3)
```

```powershell
python tools/verify.py        # exact rebuild: image, header, relocations (~10 s)
python tools/difftest.py      # every differential suite in tests/ (ASM in Unicorn vs C)
python tools/where.py 107B    # source line for a code offset (ds:XXXX for data)
python tools/graph.py 107B    # callers, callees, ports, interrupts, DATA of a routine
python tools/hostbuild.py     # native SDL3 build -> build/host/pre2.exe
build\host\pre2.exe --assets assets             # play
build\host\pre2.exe --assets assets --smoke 45  # bounded integration check (docs/smoke-test.md)
build\host\pre2.exe --assets assets --smoke 75 --scenario warp   # also ending, gameover, castle
python tests/_vga_kat.py                         # VGA model known-answer checks
python tools/coverage.py                        # routine coverage (after PRE2_COVERAGE=1 difftest)
```

Port status, content inventory and evidence: docs/completeness.md.

Prerequisites: Python 3.10+ with `capstone` and `unicorn` (pip), MSYS2 mingw64 gcc,
the private original assets in `assets/` and the DOS tools in `toolchain/`
(metadata/*.json pins every file by hash).

## Layout

- `src/MODULE1..4.ASM` - the program in link order: four link modules (relocation order
  and alignment evidence, docs/executable.md); MODULE1 also holds the stack and all DATA.
- `include/` - shared constants (record field offsets, sizes) as they are recovered.
- `c/` - the C translation on the original memory model (docs/architecture.md), platform
  models for VGA and DOS files; `c/pre2_sym.h` is generated from the ASM labels.
- `tests/` - differential suites (`tools/difftest.py`).
- `tools/` - build/verify, address lookup, symbol maintenance (`rename.py`, `define.py`,
  `symtab.py`, `apply.py` for worker proposals), static analysis (`explore.py`,
  `segflow.py`, `graph.py`), the bounded execution harness (`emu.py`) and C build.
- `host/` - the native SDL3 platform: interrupts at the game's polling points, VGA
  presentation, Sound Blaster audio, keyboard.
- `docs/` - the oracle boundary (executable.md), architecture, timing model, smoke test,
  worker briefs, next work.
- `metadata/` - pinned inputs, oracle manifest, toolchain and SDL3 locks.

Names, labels and module files are modern reconstructions; original identifiers are
unknown. Original assets and historical tool binaries are private local inputs.

# Magic Maze Web

> A simple, low-tech, monster-bashing maze game — now playable in your browser.
> Originally inspired by Gauntlet II on the Atari ST, where Kent first started
> building it as a 12-year-old in 1990.

This is a faithful HTML5 Canvas port of [Kent Dahl](https://github.com/kentdahl)'s
*Magic Maze* — a maze game with a 30+ year history across four implementations,
three languages, and one stubborn idea that wouldn't let go.

**Play it:** https://magicmaze.dfault.it/

**Not to be confused with** [the 2017 cooperative board game of the same name](https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/209778/magic-maze) by Kasper Lapp. Different game, same name.

---

## What is Magic Maze?

You play an old wizard searching the dungeon-tower of an evil demon to rescue a
captive maiden. Walk through the maze, fight (or flee from) monsters, collect
keys to open colored doors, find treasure, manage your energy and mana, and
make it to the exit on each of the ten increasingly nasty levels.

It's tile-based. It's top-down. It's pixel art. It runs at 320×200. The view is
five tiles by five tiles. There are spells. There are potions. There is a
chunky death sound when you finally lose your last hit point. The whole thing
fits the entire spirit of early-90s home computer gaming into about 1,400 lines
of code.

---

## A brief history

**1990–91 — Atari ST.** Kent, age 12, starts building Magic Maze on his Atari
ST after spending too much time playing Gauntlet II. One playable level
exists. The disk goes missing somewhere along the way and is presumed lost in
an attic.

**1994–96 — DOS / Turbo Pascal.** Kent rebuilds the game from scratch in Turbo
Pascal 7.0 for DOS. Mode 13h VGA graphics, Gravis Ultrasound for audio,
custom sprite and map formats, a built-in map editor. Released as freeware in
1996. The original Pascal source and a playable Win98-compatible binary are
still archived at:
[https://www.pvv.ntnu.no/~kentda/ancient/geocities/coding/mmaze/](https://www.pvv.ntnu.no/~kentda/ancient/geocities/coding/mmaze/)

**2004–2024 — Ruby / SDL2.** Kent ports the game to Ruby with SDL2 bindings,
adds modernized PNG sprite art, a TrueType font (Fraktur Modern), proper
joystick support, and command-line options for fullscreen, scaling, and
sound. Maintained on GitHub:
[https://github.com/kentdahl/magic_maze](https://github.com/kentdahl/magic_maze)

The Ruby port gets packaged for Debian by Joe Nahmias and Petter Reinholdtsen
and ships in every Debian release from buster through sid:
[https://packages.debian.org/sid/magicmaze](https://packages.debian.org/sid/magicmaze)
(also available on Ubuntu — see the
[Ubuntu manpage](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/bionic/man6/magicmaze.6.html)).

Kent also archives historical builds (OLPC XO-1, 32-bit Windows, original
Turbo Pascal) on itch.io:
[https://menthal.itch.io/magic-maze](https://menthal.itch.io/magic-maze)

**2026 — HTML5 / JavaScript.** This repo. A web port by Kent's brother
([Daniel Dahl](https://danieldahl.com)), who was the level designer and
tester for the original 1996 game and the 2004 Ruby port. Built with the
help of [Claude](https://claude.ai) by reverse-engineering the original
Pascal source, extracting the original sprites, sounds, and level files, and
re-implementing the game logic in vanilla JavaScript with HTML5 Canvas.

---

## Project goals

This port aims for **faithfulness over modernization**. The game looks, feels,
and plays the way the 1996 version did — same 320×200 resolution, same chunky
pixel art, same sounds, same level layouts, same monster AI, same UI.
Modernization is limited to what's needed to make it run in a browser:
- Canvas 2D instead of mode 13h VGA
- Web Audio instead of Gravis Ultrasound
- ES modules instead of Turbo Pascal units
- localStorage instead of `MM_SAV.GAM`
- CSS scaling so it fills modern displays at integer multiples (2x, 3x, 4x, 5x)

No new content. No reworked graphics. No "remastered" anything. Just the same
game, on a more modern platform.

---

## How it works

The repo contains:

```
magic-maze-web/
├── index.html            Entry point
├── style.css             Page chrome + Fraktur Modern @font-face + canvas scaling
├── js/                   Game code — vanilla ES modules, no build step
│   ├── main.js               Bootstrap, asset loading, fixed-tick frame loop
│   ├── engine.js             State, lifecycle, per-tick orchestrator
│   ├── player.js             Pickup + arrow movement (door unlock)
│   ├── combat.js             Attack spells + monster AI
│   ├── modes.js              Heal/Mana/Map/Look-ahead/Help/Confirm modes
│   ├── flow.js               Title screen, level transitions, end sequence
│   ├── render.js             Canvas drawing for every mode
│   ├── input.js              Keyboard handler with isPressed() / lastPress
│   ├── audio.js              Web Audio: SFX playback, gesture-gated context
│   ├── levels.js             Level loading, monster extraction, tile accessor
│   └── assets.js             Sprite sheet, palette, image loading
├── assets/                Game art and sound (extracted from 1996 originals)
├── levels/                Ten levels, parsed from MM_MAP.001..010
├── tools/
│   └── extract_assets.py     Reproducible asset extraction from the 1996 game
├── reference/             Source-of-truth archive
│   ├── MMAZE.PAS                Kent's original Turbo Pascal source (1996)
│   ├── MMMAPED.PAS              The map editor source
│   ├── BRIEF.md                 Architectural notes from the porting process
│   ├── README.original.md       The pre-publication README draft
│   ├── ABOUT.txt                Repo metadata reference
│   ├── mm_src.zip               Original DOS source archive
│   ├── mmaze.zip                Original DOS playable archive
│   ├── magic_maze_assets.zip    Pre-extracted assets snapshot
│   └── fraktur-modern.zip       Original font archive
├── IDEAS.md               Future enhancements (not yet implemented)
├── LICENSE                MIT
└── README.md              This file
```

Vanilla JavaScript. Native ES modules. No build step. No dependencies. Drop
the folder on any static host (or open `index.html` over `file://` once browsers
allow that for local module loading) and it runs.

### Asset extraction

The art, sounds, and levels you play with are bit-for-bit the originals from
1996, just transcoded into modern container formats (PNG, WAV, JSON). The
extraction is fully reproducible — `tools/extract_assets.py` reads the
original Turbo Pascal binaries (`MM_SPR.DAT`, `MM_*.GRA`, `MM_MAP.001..010`,
`MM_SAM.001..004`) and emits the assets used by the engine.

If you want to verify the assets match the original game, the source archives
ship with this repo under `reference/mm_src.zip` and `reference/mmaze.zip`,
and are also available from
[Kent's PVV page](https://www.pvv.ntnu.no/~kentda/ancient/geocities/coding/mmaze/).
Extract them next to the script and re-run it.

---

## Controls

| Action | Key |
|---|---|
| Move / turn | Arrow keys |
| Cast spell | Ctrl |
| Cycle attack spell | Alt |
| Heal | H (hold — drains mana) |
| Summon mana | N (hold — drains energy) |
| Magic map | M |
| Look ahead | L |
| Restart level | F9 |
| Save game | F5 |
| Load game | F4 |
| Sound on/off | S |
| Volume | PgUp / PgDn |
| Help | F1 |
| Quit | F10 / Alt+Q |
| Cancel modal / dismiss | Esc |
| Confirm Yes / No | Y / N |

Touch controls for mobile are planned for a future iteration.

---

## Building & running locally

There's nothing to build. To run locally:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/dahlskebank/magic-maze-web.git
cd magic-maze-web
python3 -m http.server 8000
# Then open http://localhost:8000 in a browser
```

A local HTTP server is needed because ES modules don't load over `file://` in
most browsers.

---

## Credits

**Original game** — Kent Dahl ([@kentdahl](https://github.com/kentdahl)),
across all implementations (Atari ST 1990–91, Turbo Pascal 1994–96, Ruby/SDL2
2004–2024, and assets re-used here):

- **Idea, design & coding:** Kent Dahl
- **Graphics design:** Kent Dahl
- **Level design:** Kent Dahl, Daniel Dahl
- **Game testing:** Per Ejnar Thomsen (original), Randi Rørvik (Ruby port), Daniel Dahl (original & Ruby port)

**Web port (this repo):** [Daniel Dahl](https://danieldahl.com), with
[Claude](https://claude.ai) as a pair-programming and reverse-engineering
assistant.

**Debian packaging of the Ruby port:** Joe Nahmias, Petter Reinholdtsen.

**Font:** Fraktur Modern by Robert Pfeffer (free), as used in the Ruby port.

---

## Roadmap

Future-only enhancements that aren't in the 1996 Pascal source are tracked
in [IDEAS.md](./IDEAS.md). Pull requests welcome — but please flag whether a
change is Pascal-faithful or a deliberate addition.

---

## Related Magic Maze resources

- **Original Pascal source & DOS binary (1996):** [pvv.ntnu.no/~kentda/ancient/geocities/coding/mmaze](https://www.pvv.ntnu.no/~kentda/ancient/geocities/coding/mmaze/)
- **Ruby/SDL2 port (2004–present):** [github.com/kentdahl/magic_maze](https://github.com/kentdahl/magic_maze)
- **itch.io (multiple historical builds):** [menthal.itch.io/magic-maze](https://menthal.itch.io/magic-maze)
- **Debian package:** [packages.debian.org/sid/magicmaze](https://packages.debian.org/sid/magicmaze)
- **Ubuntu manpage:** [manpages.ubuntu.com/.../magicmaze.6](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/bionic/man6/magicmaze.6.html)
- **Le Bottin des Jeux Linux (FR):** [download.tuxfamily.org/.../Magic_Maze](https://download.tuxfamily.org/sdtraces/BottinHTML/Bottin_K-O_files/Magic_Maze-11845.html)
- **uvlist.net entry:** [uvlist.net/game-183221](https://www.uvlist.net/game-183221-Magic+Maze)

---

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

The original game's freeware terms apply to the 1996 binary distribution.
The original Turbo Pascal source under [reference/](./reference/) (MMAZE.PAS,
MMMAPED.PAS) retains Kent's original freeware terms. The Ruby port is
dual-licensed under GPL v2 / Ruby's license. The Fraktur Modern font
([assets/fraktmod.ttf](./assets/fraktmod.ttf)) ships under its own license —
see [assets/license.txt](./assets/license.txt). This web port is released
under MIT with Kent's blessing — he gave the green light to do "whatever I
wanted" with it.

---

originally inspired by playing Gauntlet II on the Atari ST.* — the official
tagline, unchanged across every port since 2004.

# ResPaw: robot, conversación y memoria

La nueva implementación se publica con [licencia MIT](LICENSE). El
[alcance de la licencia](NOTICE) conserva las licencias de terceros y no
relicencia los archivos originales recuperados ni la tesis.

La arquitectura objetivo separa **Mega = cuerpo**, **Pico W = conectividad** y
**ResPaw Server/Companion = conversación y memoria**. El servidor puede alojarse
en una Raspberry y usar un modelo local o, con un proveedor configurado, uno en
nube. El código actual y las conexiones pendientes se distinguen en estas guías:

- [Arquitectura, responsabilidades y protocolo](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Roadmap y pruebas de integración](docs/ROADMAP.md)
- [Servidor de enlace desplegado en Raspberry](docs/server-link.md)
- [Conversación GPT, memoria y voz en Raspberry](docs/companion-raspberry.md)
- [Gateway Wi-Fi y setup desde el celular](pico/source/respaw-gateway/README.md)
- [Verificación del servidor y del Pico, 3 de octubre](docs/verificacion-enlace-2026-10-03.md)

La primera versión del acompañante conversa en español, recupera recuerdos
autorizados entre sesiones y permite corregirlos u olvidarlos. El modo local
se ejecuta en el Mac con Ollama; el Mega 2560 conserva el control de la pantalla
TFT de 3,5 pulgadas y del hardware del robot.

- [Uso y arquitectura del acompañante offline](docs/offline-companion.md)
- [Estado del arte y decisiones de memoria/RAG](docs/estado-del-arte-2026.md)
- [Resultados de verificación local](docs/verificacion-local-2026-09-13.md)
- [Carga y verificación del Mega por USB](docs/verificacion-hardware-2026-09-14.md)
- [Mejoras de conversación y memoria semántica](docs/mejoras-memoria.md)
- [Firmware Mega v2 y protocolo USB](mega2560/source/respaw-v2/README.md)
- [Receptor Pico W y cableado con el Mega](pico/source/respaw-v2/README.md)
- [Acompañamiento autónomo con Mega, pantalla y presión](mega2560/source/respaw-autonomo/README.md)
- [Carga y verificación del Mega autónomo](docs/verificacion-autonomo-2026-09-14.md)

Para funcionar sin una computadora, el firmware **respaw-autonomo** ofrece
opciones por presión y aprende preferencias guardadas en la EEPROM del Mega.
Es acompañamiento guiado con texto en la TFT; la conversación libre de la web
sigue necesitando una computadora. La guía del firmware autónomo explica el
montaje, la interacción y sus límites.

Con el modelo local preparado y Ollama iniciado:

```sh
make run
```

Abrir http://127.0.0.1:8765. El modo predeterminado simula la pantalla y no abre
ningún puerto USB. El modo invitado conserva la conversación solo en memoria
durante la sesión. Un perfil permite guardar mensajes propios mediante
«Recordar este mensaje» y recuperarlos en una conversación posterior.

```sh
make check       # Python, integración HTTP local, núcleo C++ y sintaxis JavaScript
make firmware    # Compila para Mega con dependencias fijadas; no carga la placa
```

La guía offline explica la preparación inicial de modelos, la voz opcional y el
enlace USB. Ese modo no descarga modelos automáticamente ni cambia de proveedor
si falla Ollama. La Raspberry usa el proveedor GPT explícito, con credenciales
privadas instaladas. Pasaron dos turnos reales, recuperación de un recuerdo
ficticio entre sesiones e instancias, generación de MP3 con ElevenLabs y
transcripción OpenAI de ese audio sintético mediante la API de producción.
El Pico nativo ya conecta por Wi-Fi y WSS a la Raspberry tras el setup móvil
y recupera el enlace después de reiniciar el servicio de enlace.
El cuerpo sigue sin disponibilidad; UART, micrófono físico y parlante están pendientes.
Los resultados están en el [informe de integración](docs/verificacion-integracion-2026-10-03.md).

## Archivo de recuperación de Pico W y Mega 2560

Captura realizada el 5 de septiembre de 2026. Todas las operaciones sobre las
placas fueron de lectura. Las memorias se leyeron dos veces y las copias fueron
comparadas antes de generar los artefactos canónicos.

## Organización del repositorio

Cada dispositivo sigue la misma separación para distinguir evidencia original
de archivos derivados:

```text
docs/                 Tesis y contraste técnico
mega2560/
  captures/           Lecturas originales de flash, EEPROM, fuses y serie
  firmware/           Imágenes canónicas restaurables
  analysis/           Desensamblados, cadenas y comparaciones
  reports/            Informes de recuperación
  source/             Fuente candidata y su procedencia
pico/
  captures/           Dos lecturas originales de la flash
  firmware/           Imagen completa y partición LittleFS
  reports/            Informes lógico y forense
  source/             Archivos visibles y código borrado recuperado
tools/                 Utilidades reproducibles de recuperación y análisis
```

## Resultado breve

### Raspberry Pi Pico W

- Placa: Pico W, RP2040 revisión B2, flash de 2 MiB.
- Firmware: MicroPython 1.26.1, compilado el 11 de septiembre de 2025.
- La REPL, USB y el modo BOOTSEL funcionan.
- La flash completa se leyó dos veces con `picotool --verify`; ambas imágenes
  son idénticas.
- El sistema de archivos en la captura original sólo contenía:
  - `max30102/__init__.py`
  - `max30102/circular_buffer.py`
- En esa captura no había `main.py` ni `boot.py`. El receptor v2 se instaló
  posteriormente y se documenta en su guía enlazada arriba.
- La búsqueda forense halló un script Python borrado completo en el offset de
  flash `0x1A9000`. Se conservó byte por byte como
  `pico/source/recovered-deleted/recovered_source_0x1A9000.py`. El nombre original ya
  no estaba disponible; por su contenido parece un `main.py` de prueba del
  MAX30102. El archivo recuperado es UTF-8 y su sintaxis Python es válida.

Artefactos principales:

- `pico/firmware/firmware-full.bin`: imagen restaurable de los 2 MiB completos.
- `pico/firmware/filesystem-littlefs.bin`: partición LittleFS cruda de 848 KiB.
- `pico/source/current/max30102/`: archivos fuente que aún eran visibles.
- `pico/source/recovered-deleted/`: fuente tallada desde espacio borrado.
- `pico/reports/logical-recovery-report.json`: recuperación lógica, archivo por archivo.
- `pico/reports/forensic-report.json`: datos de flash y evidencia forense.

### Arduino Mega 2560

- MCU confirmada por firma: ATmega2560 (`1E 98 01`).
- USB oficial Arduino: VID:PID `2341:0042`.
- Bootloader Wiring/STK500v2 funcional, versión informada `2.10`.
- Flash completa de 262,144 bytes leída dos veces. La primera pasada sólo
  recortó 738 bytes finales `FF`; todo su contenido coincide con la segunda.
- EEPROM de 4,096 bytes: completamente borrada (`FF`) y coincidente en ambas
  lecturas.
- Configuración leída dos veces: lock `CF`, low fuse `FF`, high fuse `D8`,
  extended fuse `FD`.
- Región de aplicación con datos hasta `0x0877D`; región de bootloader desde
  `0x3E000`.
- No hubo salida serie durante 15 segundos a 115200 ni a 9600 baudios. Eso no
  prueba una avería: el programa puede mostrar los mensajes sólo en la TFT o
  esperar una entrada externa.

Las cadenas conservadas en el binario indican una aplicación con TFT,
DFPlayer Mini, MAX30102, medición de 30 segundos, cálculo de BPM/SDNN/RMSSD,
clasificación `ESTRESADO / ANSIOSO`, `NEUTRO` o `RELAJADO`, hibernación y envío
de resultados al Pico W.

Posteriormente se recibió el sketch
`mega2560/source/tesis-mega2560/tesis-mega2560.ino`. Sus 17
cadenas literales significativas aparecen exactamente en la flash recuperada,
lo que lo identifica con alta confianza como la misma versión o una versión
muy cercana. La comparación reproducible está en
`mega2560/analysis/firmware-string-comparison.json` y el cruce con la tesis en
`docs/comparacion-tesis-firmware.md`. El documento original se conserva como
`docs/tesis-amir-flores.pdf`.

Artefactos principales:

- `mega2560/firmware/firmware-full.bin`: flash exacta, incluida la zona del bootloader.
- `mega2560/firmware/firmware-full.hex`: representación Intel HEX completa.
- `mega2560/firmware/application-only.hex`: aplicación sin la región del bootloader,
  adecuada para una eventual restauración por el bootloader USB.
- `mega2560/firmware/eeprom.bin` y `mega2560/firmware/eeprom.hex`: copia de EEPROM.
- `mega2560/analysis/application-disassembly.txt`: desensamblado AVR de la aplicación.
- `mega2560/analysis/analyzed-functions.json`: 144 funciones detectadas por análisis.
- `mega2560/analysis/printable-strings.json`: cadenas con sus offsets.
- `mega2560/reports/recovery-report.json`: tamaños, hashes y verificaciones.
- `mega2560/source/`: sketch recibido y documentación de procedencia.
- `docs/comparacion-tesis-firmware.md`: correspondencias, diferencias y riesgos frente
  a la arquitectura descrita en la tesis.

## Límite de la recuperación de fuente

En MicroPython los `.py` se almacenan como texto, por lo que se recuperaron
exactamente los dos archivos visibles y un script borrado. En el ATmega2560 el
sketch se guarda compilado: el `.ino/.cpp` exacto, nombres locales, estructura
original y comentarios no existen en la flash. El BIN/HEX preserva el programa
ejecutable exacto. El sketch recibido después coincide con toda la evidencia
textual recuperada, pero sin las versiones originales del toolchain y las
librerías no es posible demostrar una identidad de compilación bit por bit.

## Precaución

No flashear ninguna placa hasta copiar esta carpeta a por lo menos otro medio.
Una restauración completa del Mega que incluya bootloader y fuses debe hacerse
con un programador ISP; `application-only.hex` mantiene aparte la opción de
restaurar únicamente la aplicación por USB. Verificar siempre `SHA256SUMS`
antes de usar una copia.

# Hercules reconstruction

Reconstruct Disney's 1997 Windows Hercules as a faithful native source game,
eventually using SDL3. The original PC binaries are the evidence oracle; PSX
builds are secondary evidence. Historical compiler matching is a foundation for
that work, alongside semantic, source-graph, host, and renderer discoveries.

The goal is one game implementation. First-party code from HERCULES.EXE, TITLE,
ENG1, and ENG3 must ultimately exist as source. The finished native runtime must
not depend on those original executable modules.

`main` is the canonical integrated reconstruction. Source recovery, strict
matching, renderer evidence and platform work advance that same source tree.
Task branches are temporary and are removed after integration.

## Start here

- [Project direction](docs/project_direction.md) explains the target and proof boundaries.
- [Working contract](AGENTS.md) gives repository-wide rules.
- [Source guide](src/README.md) explains the module layout and how to look up a function's status.
- [Matching](docs/matching.md) defines accepted function evidence.
- [Workflow](docs/workflow.md) gives the short reconstruction loop.
- [Original binary architecture](docs/architecture.md), [source inventory](docs/inventory.md),
  and [toolchain](docs/toolchain.md) provide supporting context.

recovery.json remains the authoritative function matching state. Existing
FUNCTION_MATCH entries retain their strict raw-byte meaning; FUNCTION_MATCH_RELOCATED
accepts exact complete code with independently verified references. Source coverage,
semantic evidence, link closure, and runtime behavior are separate facts.

## Current evidence streams

| Area | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Historical C/C++ reconstruction | Exact function evidence with pinned VC5 tools and protected prior matches |
| TITLE, ENG1, ENG3, and host source | Recovers behavior and dependencies; incomplete source is identified as such |
| renderer_contract | Evidence-backed original interfaces and reference utilities |
| dropin_renderer and REA experiments | Bounded diagnostic work; neither defines the final game architecture |

Dated reports are historical measurements. Read current status from recovery.json
and the relevant module evidence; do not treat old counts as current state.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/pc/`, `src/title/`, `src/eng1/`, `src/eng3/` | Current reconstructed source by original PC module |
| `src/shared/` | Shared engine logic, interfaces, layouts and data owners |
| `recovery.json` | Per-function matching authority; accepted and incomplete units share `src/` |
| `config/` | Active source selection, link plans and bounded analysis recipes |
| `scripts/`, `tests/` | Analysis/build/verification tools and their regression fixtures |
| `evidence/`, `docs/` | Proof inputs, provenance and documented findings |
| `renderer_contract/` | Recovered renderer interfaces and reference utilities |
| `prototypes/`, `dropin_renderer/` | Explicit host, renderer and reconstruction experiments |
| `work/`, `candidates/`, `build/` | Ignored generated output and disposable experiments |

The old `behavioral/` and `calibration/` source directories are retired. Matching
status belongs to each function's ledger row, not its directory. See the
[cleanup record](docs/source_layout.md) for old-path lookup and proof preservation.

## Everyday commands

Use the configured Python 3.11+ environment and the pinned dependencies under
C:\tools. Put generated artifacts in ignored work/ or candidates/ directories.
The RAW and RELOCATED acceptance regression command is:

    python scripts/match.py verify --report work/strict_verification.json

To inspect current source without treating filenames as proof tiers:

    python scripts/source_status.py
    python scripts/source_status.py actor_pair_animation.c

A secondary worktree may add --original-root D:/Prog/hercules_recon to read the
primary checkout's originals. The source and recovery state still come from the
calling worktree. See [workflow](docs/workflow.md) for candidate compilation,
promotion, and source-graph diagnostics.

assets/ is immutable. Never commit original game files, extracted resources,
tool installations, generated builds, databases, or large disassemblies.

# Ishar 2 – čeština

Česká lokalizace DOS verze **Ishar 2**. Překlad vychází z angličtiny a ve hře
nahrazuje německou jazykovou variantu. Obsahuje 392 překladových jednotek,
550 herních řetězců, českou diakritiku v malých písmenech a velká Č a Ž.

**Projekt neobsahuje původní hru. Musíte vlastnit a dodat vlastní kompatibilní
kopii hry.** V Git repozitáři jsou zdrojové kódy, české překladové zdroje,
technická metadata a změny fontu. Hotový instalátor patří do **GitHub Releases**.

## Instalace hotové češtiny

1. Stáhněte **[Ishar2-Cestina-v1.1.zip](https://github.com/missingno7/ishar2-cestina/releases/download/v1.1/Ishar2-Cestina-v1.1.zip)** z [Releases](https://github.com/missingno7/ishar2-cestina/releases). Archiv „Source code“ je pro vývojáře.
2. ZIP rozbalte a spusťte `Ishar2-Cestina.exe` (64bitové Windows).
3. Ukončete hru. Vyberte její složku obsahující `START.EXE` a klikněte na
   **Aplikovat češtinu**.
4. Hru spusťte obvyklým způsobem v DOSBoxu a zvolte **3 – Čeština**.

Instalátor je přenosný, nevyžaduje Python, .NET ani instalaci dalších knihoven.
Potřebuje oprávnění k zápisu do složky hry. Před změnou ověří verzi a vytvoří
zálohu devíti souborů v `.ishar2-cs-backup-v1.1`. Tlačítko **Obnovit originál**
vrátí původní soubory. Zálohu proto nemažte. Uložené pozice, konfigurace
DOSBoxu ani herní EXE se nemění.

Změny vydání shrnuje [přehled v1.1](docs/RELEASE-v1.1.md).

**Přechod z v1.0:** nejprve použijte tlačítko **Obnovit originál** v instalátoru v1.0. Potom aplikujte v1.1. Nový instalátor úmyslně nepřepisuje soubory jiné verze češtiny; alternativou je vlastní čistá instalace hry. Starý instalátor zůstává dostupný v [releasu v1.0](https://github.com/missingno7/ishar2-cestina/releases/tag/v1.0).

## Stav a podporovaná verze

Aktuální verze je **v1.1**, s opravami překladu, zarovnání a plnými názvy. Podporovaná je ověřená DOS verze
obsahující angličtinu, francouzštinu a němčinu. Shoda se určuje přesnými
SHA-256 součty v [`metadata/profile.json`](metadata/profile.json), nikoli
podle názvu obchodu nebo adresáře. Jiná vydání či dříve upravené prostředky
instalátor odmítne; pro jiné verze zatím není připravená migrace.

Instalace, obnova a shoda výsledných souborů s v1.1 byly otestovány na kopiích
hry. Provedené technické testy nenahrazují odehrání hry. Celý překlad a
opravené intro stále potřebují ověření hraním v DOSBoxu. EXE není digitálně
podepsaný.

Známá omezení:

- **Č a Ž** zůstávají velká s diakritikou. **Ú → ú**, **Š → š**, **Á → A**.
  Ostatní nepodporovaná velká písmena ztrácejí diakritiku. Čisté překladové
  zdroje zůstávají ve správné Unicode češtině; změny probíhají jen při exportu.
- Běžné řádky dodržují původní délky. U 23 výslovně schválených míst
  sestavovač přesune delší text do přidaného bloku. Neověřené prodlužování odmítá.
- Písmo a některé popisky jsou společné, takže úpravy ovlivní i ostatní
  jazykové volby. Češtinu vybírejte číslem 3.
- Nápisy zapečené do grafiky nebo dosud nenalezené texty mohou zůstat původní.

## Sestavení ze zdrojových kódů

Potřebujete **Python 3.10+**, **MinGW-w64 pro Windows x64** (`g++`, `windres`)
a vlastní **neupravenou kompatibilní instalaci**. Běžné sestavení používá
jen standardní knihovnu Pythonu; Pillow je volitelné pro práci s PNG fontů.

Z kořene repozitáře:

```powershell
python tools/project.py check
python tools/project.py build --game-dir "D:\MojeHry\ISHAR2"
```

Kompilátor musí být v `PATH`. Cesty lze zadat také přes `--cxx` a `--windres`,
například `--cxx "C:\msys64\mingw64\bin\g++.exe"` a
`--windres "C:\msys64\mingw64\bin\windres.exe"`.

Vznikne `build/Ishar2-Cestina.exe`, `dist/Ishar2-Cestina-v1.1.zip` a
`dist/SHA256SUMS.txt`. **K releasu přiložte ZIP a kontrolní součty.** Adresáře
`build/` a `dist/` necommitujte. Sestavení původní instalaci nijak nepřepisuje.
Podrobnosti jsou v [návodu pro vývoj](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) a
[postupu vydání](docs/RELEASING.md).

## Úpravy překladu a fontů

- [`translation/cs.json`](translation/cs.json): čistý český text `cs` a kratší
  herní řádky `lines[].cs`, propojené stabilními ID.
- [`translation/glossary.json`](translation/glossary.json): české termíny,
  povolené tvary a jednotky, kde se mají používat.
- [`translation/font-delta.json`](translation/font-delta.json): pouze změny
  jednotlivých pixelů 15 glyfů, nikoli kompletní původní font ani hotové PNG.
- [`metadata/`](metadata/): verze, kontrolní součty, adresy textových slotů,
  jejich limity a odkazy na původní texty bez jejich obsahu.

Anglické, německé a francouzské reference se importují teprve z vlastní hry:

```powershell
python tools/project.py import --game-dir "D:\MojeHry\ISHAR2"
```

Vzniklý `.local/context.json` je soukromý pracovní podklad. **Nepřidávejte ho
do Gitu ani k releasu.** Stejně platí pro vyexportované fontové PNG.
Postup s obrázky a zadáním pro AI popisuje [vývojový návod](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
Překlad má dodržovat [jazykový styl](docs/TRANSLATION_STYLE.md) a [návaznosti textů](docs/TEXT_CONTEXT.md).

## Co patch mění

Upravuje devět prostředků: `MESSAGED.IO`, `TEXTIND.IO`, `PRESENT.IO`,
`MAIN.IO`, `GERDEP.IO`, `TABLEAU.IO`, `MAP.IO`, `MARCHAND.IO`, `TAVERNE.IO`.
Mění texty, pixely českých glyfů a pozici jednoho řádku dialogu. EXE se
nepatchuje. U 23 delších textů vloží přesměrování a připojí nové bloky;
původní adresy ostatních instrukcí zůstávají zachované. Tři prostředky se zvětší.

Instalátor rozbalí původní data z uživatelovy hry, aplikuje rozdíly a sestaví
nové prostředky. `PRESENT.IO` znovu komprimuje do A1, aby se vyhnul chybě
načítání velkého nekomprimovaného souboru. Balíček nepotřebuje obsahovat celé
původní nebo upravené `.IO` soubory. Viz [technický popis](docs/FORMAT.md).

## Hlášení chyb

Použijte **Issues** tohoto repozitáře. Uveďte verzi češtiny, zda jde o překlad
nebo instalátor, místo ve hře a postup reprodukce. U překlepu připište text
nebo ID jednotky; u instalátoru přesné znění chyby a verzi Windows.
U zobrazení ve hře pomůže verze DOSBoxu a malý snímek dotčeného místa.
Nepřikládejte celou hru, EXE, herní prostředky ani extrahovaný korpus.

## Licence

Vlastní kód patcheru a nástrojů je pod **MIT**. Tato licence se automaticky
nevztahuje na překlad, odvozené změny fontů ani původní obsah hry.
Přesný rozsah popisuje [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).

## Podpora projektu

Čeština je a zůstane zdarma. Stažení ani používání není podmíněné platbou.
Pokud se vám projekt líbí a chcete podpořit vznik dalších překladů, source
portů a projektů kolem starých her, můžete mě dobrovolně podpořit na
[Patreonu](https://www.patreon.com/cw/JiriVestfy).

# CSBweb

Dungeon Master and Chaos Strikes Back, in the browser, written in TypeScript.

## About

CSBweb makes Dungeon Master (the original Atari ST version) and its sequel playable on
anything with a web browser, from the original game data files.

Its engine is ported from CSBWin, Paul R. Stevens' C++ version of the game, which he wrote
by disassembling the Atari ST binary. CSBWin's source is still the specification for how
the game plays. The timers, the monsters, the spells and the formulas follow it, in the
same order and with the same numbers. The functions ported from it keep its names, so a
behaviour can be traced from one codebase to the other. The code around them is the
port's own: its structure, and everything CSBWin never had, from the browser and touch
screens to the save dialog, players' own dungeons and the site. Where the port departs
from CSBWin on purpose, `DEBT.md` lists each departure and the reason for it.

Every FTL dungeon plays, and so do the fans' dungeons the welcome page lists. A player can
also add a dungeon of their own. Saves are CSBWin's own files, so a game moves between the
two.

Play it at <https://csbweb.looten.net/>, the reference instance, or set up your own with
[doc/SETUP.md](doc/SETUP.md).

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 (`.nvmrc`)
- `7z` (7-Zip or p7zip), for the two fetch commands
- `npm run fetch-csbwin-src` once: it fetches `doc/CSBwin-src/`, CSBWin's C++ source, which
  the docs cite and `npm test` reads
- `npm run fetch-gamefiles` once: it fetches the original game files and the fans' dungeons
  into `tools/fixtures/gamefiles/`, one directory per data set listed in
  `tools/data-sets.json`, from dmweb.free.fr, Paul R. Stevens' site and the Dungeon Master
  forum's shared OneDrive. The tests and the dev server read them
- Google Chrome, for the golden frames

### Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run dev            # Vite dev server on http://localhost:9000
npm run build          # tsc, then vite build into dist/, and the server's module into dist/server/
npm start              # the server, over dist/
npm test               # tsc and every asserting tool in tools/
npm test -- --frames   # ...and the golden frames
```

`npm test` is the gate: `tsc --noEmit` type-checks what `vite build` alone would not.

## Project Structure

```
csbweb/
├── src/                   # TypeScript source; CLAUDE.md → "Code layout" has the map
│   ├── core/              # binary reads, decompression, image decoding, object ids
│   ├── data/              # dungeon.dat, graphics.dat and save-file readers and writers
│   ├── engine/            # the game: CSBWin's d., its systems, the main loop
│   ├── renderer/          # the 320x200 screen: viewport bytecode, the DM interface
│   ├── audio/             # samples
│   ├── ui/                # the page's DOM side, and the welcome page
│   ├── stats/             # the statistics page
│   ├── assets/            # the page's fonts, icons and the FTL logo
│   └── main.ts            # the page's bootstrap
├── server/                # the deployed server: the page, the data sets, the statistics
├── tools/                 # verification tools (checks/), the golden frames, the fetch commands
├── tools/fixtures/        # CSBWin saves the tools read; gamefiles/, the data sets (not ours, fetched)
├── utils/                 # the maintainer's scripts: deploying, backups, the official games installed, the forum's dungeons submitted
```

# Duke Nukum v2.0 — source

The complete C and assembly source of **Duke Nukum** v2.0 (Apogee, 1991; the first
Duke Nukem), episodes 1–3, reconstructed from the original executables, and an SDL3
port that plays it on a modern PC.

* **`src/`** is the game.  Compiled with the original toolchain (Turbo C 2.0, TASM 1.0,
  TLINK 2.0, LZEXE 0.91) it produces `DN1.EXE`, `DN2.EXE` and `DN3.EXE` **byte for byte**;
  the original files are the oracle that proves it.
* **`port/`** runs that same source on Windows (and later Linux/macOS) through SDL3: one
  `duke1.exe` plays all three episodes, chosen in a dialog drawn with the game's own
  routines.

The game files (the original executables, graphics, levels) are not part of this
repository and must never be committed or redistributed; put your own copy in `assets/`
(ignored by git) to build and test.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`src/`](src/README.md) | the game: `GAME1.C`, `GAME2.C` (the two original translation units), `DUKE.H`, `TOOLBOX.ASM`, `BUILD.BAT` |
| [`port/`](port/README.md) | the SDL3 port: emulated PC (EGA, timer, keyboard, PC speaker, DOS) and the launcher |
| `tools/` | build and check tools (Python) |
| `config/` | pinned toolchain, compiler profile, SHA-256 of the original executables |
| [`docs/`](docs) | [actors](docs/actors.md), [the port's design](docs/sdl3-port.md), [the original executables](docs/originals.md), [editing src/ without changing the binaries](docs/turbo-c.md) |

## Build

The original executables, from `src/`, compared with the originals in `assets/`:

```
python tools/build.py            # dn1/dn2/dn3: EQUAL = byte for byte
```

The SDL3 port (MinGW-w64 gcc and SDL3, see `port/README.md`):

```
cmake -S port -B build/port -G "MinGW Makefiles"
cmake --build build/port
build/port/duke1.exe --data assets
```

Everything at once — originals present, DOS build equal, port builds and its EGA
self-test passes:

```
python tools/validate.py
```

## Working on the source

Any change to `src/` must keep `tools/build.py` EQUAL: the source is the original program,
not a version of it.  Turbo C's code generation decides what "the same program" means in
detail (register allocation, block order, data layout, the order of uninitialised data by
name hash); [docs/turbo-c.md](docs/turbo-c.md) lists the rules.  Renames go through
`tools/rename.py`, which keeps them safe.  Port-specific behaviour belongs in `port/`
(platform code and `port/override/`), never in `src/`.

History: the per-function reconstruction that led here is preserved in git (tag
`matching-archive`).

# DuckTales historical reconstruction

This repository bootstraps a matching reconstruction of the original DOS
**Disney's DuckTales: The Quest for Gold**. The target is historical C/ASM,
native object contributions, ordered relocations, overlays and eventually the
packed executable. An SDL port is outside this milestone.

The supplied originals in ignored `assets/` are immutable. Their inventory,
identities and extracted structure are pinned in `layout/oracle.lock.json`.
Every verification regenerates expectations from those originals and compares
them to the lock. No verification command updates the lock.

The bootstrap identifies an EXEPACK root and ten appended MZ overlays, plus
16 resource containers with 400 raw entries. Original-stub emulation verifies
the independent root decoder. MSC 5.10-family runtime evidence is strongest;
MSC 5.00 and 6.00 remain tested alternatives. Three complete CRT members have
strict runtime ownership. Two symbolic C/ASM examples reproduce complete code
regions, with original translation-unit/object bindings still unresolved.

There is **no complete reconstructed game build yet**. Accepted game C/ASM
bytes are zero. The single authoritative current accounting is generated
`build/status.json`; `build/validation.json` records the latest fresh bootstrap
validation. See [setup](docs/setup.md), [proof rules](docs/methodology.md),
[toolchain evidence](evidence/toolchain.md), [EXEPACK/overlays](evidence/exepack-overlays.md)
and [resource evidence](evidence/resource-containers.md).

Run from the repository root with the pinned tools available:

```powershell
python tools/oracle.py verify
python tools/validate.py
python tools/context.py root 0x8410 --length 0x26
python tools/context.py --list
python tools/overlays.py
```

For one bounded candidate, put the complete source in ignored worker scratch:

```powershell
python tools/historical.py build/workers/example/candidate.c --profile msc510-medium-size
python tools/inspect_omf.py build/search/run-REPLACE/PROBE.OBJ
python tools/match.py build/search/run-REPLACE/PROBE.OBJ root 0x8410 0x8426 --segment PROBE_TEXT
```

Use the fresh directory printed by the compiler. `CODE_BYTES_EXACT` is a
diagnostic code gate; it cannot promote a source or waive declarations, other
storage, FIXUPPs, original TU membership or linked bindings. Overlay context
and matching use module-local offsets; reports preserve encoded shared-arena
relocation coordinates too.

`tools/` contains deterministic analysis, historical compile/link probes,
OMF inspection, matching and validation. `layout/` contains identities and
ownership. `evidence/` retains reviewed conclusions and reproducible source
probes. `tests/` exercises malformed inputs and proof gates. All generated
objects, disassembly, extracted originals and worker scratch belong under
ignored `build/`. Accepted `src/`, `asm/`, `include/` and module recipes will
be added when their contribution proof exists.

# Ultima V in SDL

A port of *Ultima V: Warriors of Destiny* (the 1988 DOS version) to C++ and SDL2, made from the
decompiled original. It plays the whole game - title sequence, character creation, towns,
dungeons, combat, magic, the endings - using the original game's data files, and can stand in
for three of the original graphics drivers: EGA, CGA and Hercules.

**You need your own copy of the original game, and it must be the IBM PC (MS-DOS) version.**
Ultima V was released for many machines - Apple II, Commodore 64 and 128, Atari ST, Amiga, NES,
PC-98 and others - and their files are in different formats that this port cannot read. Only the
files of the IBM PC release work. This repository contains no pictures, maps or sound from the
game; the port reads them from the game directory at run time.

## Screenshots

| EGA | Hercules (green screen) |
|---|---|
| ![EGA](docs/ega.png) | ![Hercules, green](docs/hercules-green.png) |

<!-- Placeholders: put ega.png and hercules-green.png in docs/screenshots/. -->

## Requirements

- The files of the **IBM PC (MS-DOS) version** of the game in one directory. You can tell it is
  the right version by these files: `ULTIMA.EXE`, `DATA.OVL` and the other `*.OVL` overlays,
  `EGA.DRV`, `CGA.DRV`, `HER.DRV`, `TILES.16`, `TILES.4`, `BRIT.DAT`, `SAVED.GAM`. If the game came
  on several floppy disks, copy the contents of all of them into the one directory. File names
  may be upper or lower case. Files from any other platform's release will not work.
- A C++17 compiler (`g++`) and `make`.
- SDL2 development files. On Debian, Ubuntu or WSL: `sudo apt install build-essential libsdl2-dev`

## Build

```
make build/u5sdl
```

Everything that is built goes to `build/`.

## Run

```
build/u5sdl /path/to/ultima5
```

or `make run GAME=/path/to/ultima5`.

It starts like the original: the Origin logo, Lord British's signature, the title, then the demo
and the main menu (Journey Onward, Create New Character, Transfer from Ultima IV, Introduction,
Acknowledgements). The game directory is never written to: saved games go to `./u5save`
(change it with `-w`). A saved game already in the game directory is used until you save.

### Options

```
build/u5sdl [-v ega|cga|herc] [-p green|amber|white] [-4] [-s scale] [-j | -m] [-w save dir] <game dir>
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-v ega` | 16 colours, 320×200 (the default) |
| `-v cga` | 4 colours, 320×200 |
| `-v herc` | Hercules monochrome, 640×300; `-v hercraw` shows its dots unblended |
| `-p green\|amber\|white` | colour of the Hercules monitor (default green) |
| `-o` | user original resolutiono. If not, stretch the picture to 4:3, as a PC monitor showed it |
| `-s n` | window scale (default 3) |
| `-m` | skip the title sequence and start at the menu |
| `-j` | skip the menu too: Journey Onward with the saved game |
| `-w dir` | where saved games are written (default `./u5save`) |

Examples:

```
build/u5sdl -4 /path/to/ultima5              # EGA, 4:3
build/u5sdl -v herc /path/to/ultima5         # Hercules on a green screen
build/u5sdl -v herc -p amber /path/to/ultima5
build/u5sdl -v cga -j /path/to/ultima5       # CGA, straight into the saved game
```

### Keys

The keys are the original's.

- **Arrow keys** move (Shift + keypad also works).
- **Letters** are the commands: `A`ttack, `B`oard, `C`ast, `E`nter, `F`ire, `G`et, `H`ole up,
  `I`gnite torch, `J`immy, `K`limb, `L`ook, `M`ix, `N`ew order, `O`pen, `P`ush, `Q`uit and save,
  `R`eady, `S`earch, `T`alk, `U`se, `V`iew, `X`-it, `Y`ell, `Z`tats.
- **0-6** set the active player. **Space** passes a turn.
- **Ctrl-S** switches the sound on and off. **Ctrl-E** exits; closing the window quits too.
- In dungeons: left and right turn, up advances, down backs up.

`Q` saves the game; nothing is saved when you just close the window.

## Tests

```
make check GAME=/path/to/ultima5
```

builds and runs the headless tests in `build/`. They play scripted parts of the game against the
real data files and leave screenshots (`build/*.ppm`) and logs there.

## Layout

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/` | the ported game and the SDL front end (`sdl_main.cpp`, `sdl_platform.cpp`) |
| `test/` | headless tests and their scripted platform |
| `build/` | binaries and test output (not in git) |
| `docs/screenshots/` | pictures for this page |

`src/data.cpp` and `src/data.h` are generated from the game's `DATA.OVL` by the reverse-engineering
project's `gen_data.py`; they are not edited by hand.

## Not included

- The Tandy driver (`T1K.DRV`).
- The original's disk-swap prompts and copy to hard disk: the port reads one directory.
